summary: The narrator, Morgan, visits fertility doctor Hannah Klein after a final intrauterine insemination with Steve's sperm failed, confirming she will not have a biological child. Klein suggests considering adoption, and Morgan, though grieving, feels a sense of liberation at no longer having to endure the repeated humiliation of treatment. The passage is a reflective, wry excerpt from a fiction work and opens with a reference to Carly Grove, who found Kevin quickly and easily.
one_line: Morgan learns her final fertility treatment has failed and considers adoption after a visit to Dr. Hannah Klein.
key_facts: The narrator Morgan's final attempt at intrauterine insemination (IUI) with Steve's deposit had failed.
Morgan describes IUI as med-speak for an expensive "turkey baster."
Morgan confirmed her pregnancy suspicions with a pregnancy test run by Hannah Klein's assistant, Lori.
Hannah Klein's office is on the Upper West Side.
Hannah Klein was pushing seventy and was a chain smoker.
Hannah Klein is a child of the Holocaust.
Hannah Klein told Morgan, "maybe you ought to just start considering adoption—if having a child still means that much to you."
Morgan felt strangely liberated sitting in Klein's office because she no longer had to endure repeated humiliation of treatment.
Morgan's tests showed no cysts, fibroids, polyps, or ovulatory abnormalities.
Morgan's uterus and Fallopian tubes were fine, and Steve's sperm counts were okay.
Morgan had eaten two hot dogs with sauerkraut from a striped-umbrella vendor before going to Klein's office.
Morgan mentions Carly Grove, who found Kevin in no time with zero hassles, and calls the situation mysterious.
Klein is described as having white hair in a bun and a raspy New York voice.
Morgan describes the realization as accepting that the baby part of her life is over and moving on to Plan B.
